correctness.rationale: For every nonroot internal clade v, extinction loss of its incoming unit edge occurs with probability q^{s(v)} independently and θq+(1−θ)q^{s(v)} in the common-shock mixture; the n leaves contribute no excess, yielding Δ_T=θ[(n−2)q−Σ_nonrootinternal q^{s(v)}]. Six-leaf unlabeled root splits 1+5,2+4,3+3 enumerate 3+2+1=6 shapes with nonroot clade-size multisets {2,3,4,5}, {2,2,4,5}, {2,2,3,5}, {2,2,3,4}, {2,2,3,3}, {2,2,2,4}. Adjacent polynomial gaps are q²(1−q), q³(1−q), q⁴(1−q), q³(1−q), q²(1−q)², strictly positive; hence the Δ order. E/F both have depths 2,2,3,3,3,3, and their local F gap is q²(1−q)²; all ancestor clade sizes stay constant under a depth-preserving graft. For 4 and 5 tips the stated most balanced root splits are strict optimizers. Separate independent exact small-shape enumeration checked all six clade vectors/depths and symbolic gaps. The universal result follows from factorization and linearity, not finitely sampled probabilities.
residual_risks: Independent computations are bounded and do not replace the analytical all-parameter proof.

Prior work comparison separated known baseline methods from submitted structural claim
value.rationale: Phylogenetic diversity loss and Sackin depth balance are natural ecology/tree-shape invariants. The explicit strict separation of equal-depth minimum-Sackin trees proves that balancing alone does not determine catastrophe excess loss; the graft extends a six-tip witness to arbitrary tree size without changing any leaf-depth vector. This is a motivated structural counterexample rather than an arbitrary table.
residual_risks: Applicability is limited to the theorem hypotheses, not a generalization to all related objects or interventions.

final_claim: For six-leaf rooted full binary unit-edge trees under independent Bernoulli(q) extinction versus a θ-common-shock mixture (0<q<1,0<θ≤1), the six shapes have strictly ordered excess loss Δ=θ[4q−F_T(q)], A>B>C>D>E>F. The Sackin-minimal E and F have the same leaf-depth multiset yet Δ_E−Δ_F=θq²(1−q)². Replacing E by F as any fringe preserves each labeled leaf depth and lowers excess by that amount.
limitations: Correlated-extinction phylogenetics and tree-shape optimization might contain an earlier six-tip/all-q comparison under different terminology.
The 2018 ranked-tree loss paper was not inspected in full; do not assert it fails to cover the submitted theorem.
The depth-preserving graft does not classify all optimal large trees; equal/unit branch lengths and homogeneous marginals are essential.
No external expert attestation or Lean formal proof; computations corroborate but do not establish the infinite theorem.
Publication is withheld until privacy-neutral guarded replacements for public AUDIT.json and METADATA.json are verified.
